body:
Redline round 5

Reviewed the fix diff from round 4 (dbfcd69..dd42671), and the coverage pass's candidates over the whole pull request at dd42671.

The coverage pass over the whole pull request at dd42671 returned 10 candidates: 4 confirmed, 3 for the person, 1 collapsed into findings already reported or settled, 0 already tracked, 2 dropped (refuted, outside the diff or disproportionate).

The round 4 fixes add the `\b` end anchor to the duplicate-target parse and the 'opening with the index ... anything meant for the reader after it' sentence, in both the verify prompt and the agent file. The coverage-off prompt is left untouched, and a key-phrase check pins the sentence. I traced the widened regex on the refs the prompt now invites and found no correctness bug in the fix diff. The four findings are all nits about tightness and clarity on the block's edges: two parse and escape clauses no case turns on, a comment that says Already tracked candidates are not set aside, and a duplicate line that names a finding's outcome but not its id. The repository has no routes/console.php, so no scheduled or queued work shares these files. The version stays at 0.2.2 against main's 0.2.1.

### Findings (0 correctness, 4 nit)

- **R5-1** · nit · low · confirmed · `tests/loop-test.mjs:1574` · No escaping case puts `&` inside a code span, so 'a span is left as written' is pinned for `<` only
- **R5-2** · nit · low · confirmed · `tests/loop-test.mjs:1620` · The duplicate-target parse's new `\b` end anchor and its `\s+` have no case that turns on them
- **R5-3** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:508` · LISTED_ELSEWHERE's comment says a `finding` entry covers Already tracked, but those candidates are `known` and set aside
- **R5-4** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:891` · A duplicate of a candidate that became a finding names the target's place and outcome, but not the finding's id

### For the person

- `workflows/redline-loop.js:2148` · Coverage candidate 1, traced: the block skips every `forThePerson` entry on trust that a For the person line exists. A verifier that accounts a candidate as forThePerson but writes no line leaves it as a count only. That trust is #79's accountCoverage (line 1373), not this PR, and since For the person lines carry no index there is no exact check. A count check (fewer lines than forThePerson entries gives a warning) is the cheap alternative.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:912` · Coverage candidates 2 and 5, plausible but not reproduced here (the markdown API and node are refused to the reviewer). In CommonMark a link's destination or title is parsed at `]`, before a backtick inside it is paired, so in '[a](/u "`") </details> `' blockText pairs that backtick with the last one and leaves `</details>` raw. With round 4's lone CR, this is a second gap in the hand-written pairing model. The docs' 'no tag ... can end the block' is stronger than the code. Candidate 5's alternative: keep a span unescaped only when the text holds none of `[`, `\r`, `\` or a newline, and escape the whole text otherwise.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:863` · Coverage candidate 10: the set-aside block has no heading of its own. In a round with no For the person entries it follows straight after Already tracked or Findings in the body, and after Rounds in the handoff, so a reader scanning headings sees it inside that section. docs/running.md places it 'after For the person'. Whether it gets its own heading, or sits under For the person always, is a copy choice.

<details>
<summary>Candidates set aside (3): collapsed, already tracked or dropped</summary>

- `workflows/redline-loop.js:2130` · When the reviewer returns a bare-number finding id, the id rename also rewrites a `duplicate` ref with the same text. A bare index, which R4-1 made the documented first form of a duplicate ref, becomes a finding id, and the duplicate's real target is lost. · disproportionate: Conditions: the reviewer must return a malformed finding id that is a bare number, and the same round must account for a duplicate by a bare index equal to that number. In that case the ref really is ambiguous between the two. Round 2 ruled the same rename path disproportionate.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:2156` · Duplicate refs are not checked the way `finding` refs are. Two candidates marked as duplicates of each other collapse into nothing, and the count sentence still says they collapsed into findings already reported or settled. · disproportionate: Conditions: the verifier must collapse two candidates into each other, with neither collapsing into a finding. Even then both still show in the block, each with its own summary and '(candidate N, ...: duplicate)', so neither is hidden; only the count sentence's group name is wrong for them.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:912` · Altitude: the escaping depends on a hand-written model of GitHub's inline parser (backtick runs, plus fallbacks for `\n` and backslash-backtick). Every construct the model leaves out (link destinations and titles, lone `\r`, backslash escapes) is a separate hole, each patched one special case at a time. · duplicate: 2; same cause, blockText's hand-written model of GitHub's inline parser. The simpler rule it proposes is on candidate 2's For the person line.

</details>

Each finding has an inline comment with the detail or, where GitHub could not anchor it, sits under Not placed inline below. Redline replies in the finding's thread, or in a PR comment that opens with its marker, once the round's fixes are committed.

comments.body:
**R5-1** · nit · low · confirmed

**No escaping case puts `&` inside a code span, so 'a span is left as written' is pinned for `<` only**

The escaping scenario's spans hold `<Head title="x" />`, ``a ` b <c>``, `<c>` and `<b>`, and the only `&` is in candidate 1's ref ('Tom & Jerry wrote < by hand'), outside every span. So a blockText that escaped `&` across the whole text before pairing spans would produce the same six expected lines and stay green. On GitHub, a span such as `a && b` would then show as `a && b`, the result the follow-up spec's probe recorded as wrong. The testing/tests.md bullet on pinning escaped text asks for a case per form. Traced from the six cases and the expected lines at 1590-1597.

Proposed fix: Add a candidate to the `tags` scenario whose summary holds `&` inside a span and outside it, for example cand('app/g.vue', 7, 'a span `a && b <c>` keeps its ampersands & this one does not') with an `outside` ref. Expect the line '- `app/g.vue:7` · a span `a && b <c>` keeps its ampersands & this one does not · outside: untouched code', raise the label's count to 7, and see the check red with `&` escaped before the span pairing.

**R5-2** · nit · low · confirmed

**The duplicate-target parse's new `\b` end anchor and its `\s+` have no case that turns on them**

The R4-1 fix widened the parse at workflows/redline-loop.js:2154 to `/^(?:(?:candidate|index)\s+)?(\d+)\b/i`, and the same commit range adds a testing/tests.md rule that each form gets a case seen red under a mutation of its own clause. Every duplicate ref the loop test uses ('R1-1', '3', 'candidate 2', 'index 1', 'CANDIDATE 1', '4', '99', '1; #7 tracks the case-folding') reads the same with `(\d+)` in place of `(\d+)\b`, and with `\s*` in place of `\s+`. So a ref like '1st pass missed it' would read as candidate 1, and 'candidate1' as an index, with all checks green. The R4-2 fix pinned the forms that existed when it was raised; the `\b` came after it. Traced from the regex and the test's refs.

Proposed fix: Add two entries to formsOut: { index: 7, outcome: 'duplicate', ref: '1st pass missed it' } and { index: 8, outcome: 'duplicate', ref: 'candidate1' }, with candidates for them, and check that each line ends with the ref as written and no '(candidate 1, ...)'. See the first red with `\b` removed and the second red with `\s+` changed to `\s*`.

**R5-3** · nit · low · confirmed

**LISTED_ELSEWHERE's comment says a `finding` entry covers Already tracked, but those candidates are `known` and set aside**

The comment reads 'The outcomes the round lists elsewhere: a finding under Findings or Already tracked'. But accountCoverage (line 1368) rewrites every `finding` entry whose finding carries a knownAs to `known` before the set-aside filter at line 2148 runs. So a candidate behind an Already tracked finding is never a `finding` entry there: it is set aside and listed in the block as well as under Already tracked, as the loop test's 'a known finding from a candidate is listed in the set-aside block' check expects. A reader who trusts the comment would think such a candidate is listed only under Already tracked.

Proposed fix: Reword the comment to 'a finding under Findings, an entry under For the person; a finding under Already tracked is accounted as `known` (accountCoverage), so it is set aside too and its line names the issue'.

**R5-4** · nit · low · confirmed

**A duplicate of a candidate that became a finding names the target's place and outcome, but not the finding's id**

`into` carries the target candidate's index, file, line and outcome only, so the line reads '(candidate 1, `app/x.php:3`: finding)'. The target candidate is not in the block, since findings are listed elsewhere, and the verifier may anchor the finding on another line inside the diff. With several findings, the reader cannot tell which finding the duplicate collapsed into. The target's ref, which is the finding's id after accountCoverage, is already in byIndex at line 2156. The accounting sentence allows a duplicate's ref to open with either the candidate's index or the finding's id, so this form is reachable as the prompt asks. Traced from setAsideBlock and the `into` builder.

Proposed fix: Carry the target's ref in `into` when its outcome is `finding` (and `known`, whose ref opens with the finding's id), and render it after the outcome, for example '(candidate 1, `app/x.php:3`: finding R5-2)'. Add a check to the duplicate-forms scenario with a target accounted as a finding.
